evidence: Every criterion across the 2 gates and 3 scored dimensions names a concrete browser-observable outcome with a fail clause, a working positive control before each negative, and distinctive probes chosen by the judge (unique titles/markers, payload markers joined from halves, hostile title marker, localStorage key). Durable evidence is required where state matters: cw_shared_saved_record and cw_save_reload_restart read back after clearing all origin storage and reloading; cw_save_reload_restart additionally re-reads after the real restart_app tool on a fresh page; cw_restore_request_repeat_safe and cw_history_restore_adds_revision read revisions from a freshly loaded page; stale-save rows read the record from a third page. No criterion relies on 'looks right', a source read, or a response shape without state change: cw_custom_document_surface uses enumerated read-only DOM facts (functional prompt bars implementation files, app_context.md:18-29 limits script to three named uses). Visual likerts carry 0-5 anchors and are taste-bounded. Commit 24c4a77e (functional/judge.toml cw_save_reload_restart, frozen line 379) only adds checks: the judge must note all three revisions' sources before the restart ('the second revision is the only one that carries the second marker') and after the restart open each and match, plus 'if any revision is missing or its source differs from what was noted before the restart'. Nothing became looser for the model; the old 'first revision ... original source' bar is subsumed. Weak app tried: one that keeps only the current body (or rebuilds history from the current row) on restart now fails because revision two's distinctive marker must come back; one that keeps restore idempotency only in memory adds a revision on the post-restart replay and fails. Conforming alternative tried: an app whose restore replay is refused as stale (409) instead of returning the prior result still passes, matching the public 'shouldn't create another revision' wording; the golden (server.js:95-118 restore_operations table, app.tsx:159-161 history buttons with read-only 'Historical source' pre) supports every step. Non-blocking note: the criterion tolerates a history list that omits the current revision, yet asks to 'open each of the three revisions in history'; for such an app revision three's source is still browser-decidable from the opened current record (and equals revision one), so this is wording precision (row 33 territory), not a decidability defect. Not exercised: no raw-evidence-index.json exists in the run folder and no full configured judge run of the edited criterion is cited; this row is a source-level criteria-design check and its verdict does not claim any Oracle, model or portal score.
